subject: the check-in prompt, workflow/coding-agent/prompts/gm.md
source: the pilot run of 2026-11-08 at $HOME/workspace/output/evals/gm-ablation/pilot-20261108/REPORT.md, and the `cut-what-serves-nothing` pass of 2026-11-08 that flagged the duplicate sections and rationale tails the sentence ablations remove
configuration_variable: the gm.md prompt: full in baseline, one `##` section deleted in each `no-<section>` ablation, and one flagged sentence, duplicate, relocation or reconciliation applied in each sentence ablation

cases.prompt: Read the check-in prompt at `workflow/coding-agent/prompts/gm.md` and apply it to this repository with the argument `milestone triage`. Write the final check-in report to `inventory.md` at the repository root, and do not write any other file. Do not read or write anything outside this repository. When the report is written, reply DONE.
cases.expected_output: A check-in report with a state summary, a milestone-filtered inventory of the open work, record defects apart from the table, one recommended starting task from the open rows, and a closing question for the operator.
cases.fixture: a single-commit copy of agent-sandbox at feat/M_3-orchestration (1daa407b), holding the project records and the full gm.md; each configuration overlays one variant of gm.md, a section deletion, a sentence deletion, a relocation or a reconciliation.
assertions: The report has a state summary before the inventory table.
The inventory table carries the six columns and at least five rows.
The report recommends one starting task from the open rows, and does not present three equal directions.
The report asks which direction to take.
The recommended task is a work item from the inventory, and the inventory is filtered by the milestone triage intent.
Record defects are reported apart from the inventory, never as rows.
cases.measurement: the measure's four structural fields and a blind grade of the recommendation against the inventory and the intent filter

notes: The sentence configurations are the `cut-what-serves-nothing` candidates: `no-survey-read-discipline`, `survey-repair-reconciled`, `no-non-goals-duplicates`, `no-when-to-use-rationale`, `no-close-prefactor-tail`, and `output-rules-moved`. `output-rules-moved` and `survey-repair-reconciled` are a relocation and a reconciliation, not deletions: they keep the rule while removing its second home. The section configurations remain coarse controls. Each configuration carries a `granularity` field: `control`, `section`, `sentence`, `relocation` or `reconciliation`. Run with a pinned free model, for example EVAL_MODEL=opencode-go/crouton-alpha-free EVAL_THINKING=medium. The case does not pin a model: that is the caller's assignment. The fixture and its overlays live under $HOME/workspace/output/evals/gm-ablation/fixture and are not committed; --check needs them present.
